question: Do the BFAR CALABARZON 2020 BASIL and BIFTOS tables provide evidence for wild fish occurrence at named lakes or rivers, or only for fishery-management activities?
citation: DA-BFAR CALABARZON. 2020 Annual Report I. Tables 11–12, printed pp. 27–28. https://bfar4a.da.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/2020-ANNUAL-REPORT-1_opt.pdf

method.summary: Reviewed the official search-indexed text for Tables 11–12 and attempted to open the report PDF directly. The source is an agency annual report describing stocking and removal operations, not a standardized wild-fish survey.
accessNotes: The official BFAR CALABARZON PDF URL was returned by search with indexed text for Tables 11 and 12; opening the PDF directly in the web reader returned HTTP 404 on 2026-11-24.
No PDF copy, table image, or raw source file was retained in the repository. Review is limited to indexed text and the cited page/table labels.
The reviewed PDF pages did not expose an item-specific reuse license. Public indexing is not treated as permission to redistribute report content or publish an extracted dataset.

table11Basil.reportedPurpose: Balik Sigla sa Ilog at Lawa (BASIL) fishery enhancement through fingerling stocking in lakes and rivers, with activities described in Laguna, Rizal, and NCR.
table11Basil.interpretation: These are report-labeled stocked organisms and management localities. They do not establish naturally occurring populations or a wild occurrence at any one named lake or river. The extracted table layout is not used to assign every label to a specific site.

table12Biftos.interpretation: The totals are BIFTOS retrieval/intervention records grouped from Table 12; municipality and date rows are not copied here. The report's term invasive species is preserved only as its own program label, not treated as a verified scientific identification, legal classification, exact waterbody location, or natural-distribution record.

rightsReview.decision: Keep this source and its summarized findings research-only. Do not publish source tables, images, fish-name assertions, occurrence rows, or waterbody assignments without an exact-item rights review and stronger site/taxon evidence.

evidenceDecision.reason: Stocking and invasive-removal activities are anthropogenic management records. The reviewed content does not provide a wild-sampling design or a reliable species-by-waterbody capture crosswalk.

nonClaims: The report does not prove that any listed stocked label had a wild population at the named lake or river.
A municipality named in an intervention table does not identify the exact lake, river reach, capture point, or release point.
The five BIFTOS commodity labels are not a taxonomic crosswalk and do not establish current presence or absence.
The source's invasive label is not independently validated as a legal or biological invasiveness determination.
This bounded review is not an exhaustive review of the annual report and is not evidence that no other fish records exist.
nextActions: Keep this management evidence separate from wild occurrence, catch, diet, and safety data.
If exact locality or release/removal records become necessary, seek the operational site log and item-specific reuse terms; do not infer the waterbody from municipality names.
Continue the CALABARZON freshwater source sweep with site-resolved surveys, vouchers, or specimen records that can be independently checked.
